recent_posts.title: AI for War (in minecraft)
recent_posts.summary: A developer running AI bots (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok) in Minecraft pits them against each other in war games, having them build and destroy castles autonomously. The bots write code on the fly to control their behavior, enabling destruction at inhuman speed and scale. The video also touches on real-world AI-in-weapons concerns (the Anthropic/US DoD controversy), and the author shares a candid burnout update: the project is stalling due to deep bugs in the Mineflayer framework, open-source management overhead, AI slop in pull requests, and existential discomfort about building AI that replaces human creativity. Despite this, the author commits to keeping the project alive, citing scientific value in observing AI agent behavior in safe sandboxes.

recent_posts.title: Evolution in Higher Dimensions
recent_posts.summary: A deep dive into building a system that randomly generates, mutates, and evolves mathematical functions represented as expression trees. Functions are modeled as recursive trees of operators (unary and binary), which can be grown, mutated by replacing nodes, or cross-pollinated via grafting. The system generates colorful parametric 3D surfaces and 2D patterns, implemented in JavaScript with GLSL shaders for performance. This approach is a form of symbolic regression — a genetic algorithm for function approximation — which the author compares to neuroevolutionary methods like NEAT. Interactive web toys (a Picbreeder-style pattern evolver and a 3D biomorphs tool) are published for public use. The author acknowledges symbolic regression's limitations versus neural network evolution but highlights its portability across languages.

recent_posts.title: Nature Sanctuary in stardew valley
recent_posts.summary: A developer documents a two-year experiment in Stardew Valley observing natural tree reproduction and ecosystem growth without player intervention. The forest grew from four planted saplings, with faster-reproducing species spreading more but eventually stagnating due to overcrowding. This emergent behavior inspired plans to create a game centered around autonomous, evolving ecosystems, marking a shift toward more game design content.

recent_posts.title: Math Creatures in Hyperspace
recent_posts.summary: A web-based tool for visualizing high-dimensional mathematical functions by mapping multiple inputs (U, V, time, and custom parameters) to spatial coordinates (X, Y, Z) and color values (RGB, alpha). The system allows exploration of parametric surfaces with up to 7 output dimensions and unlimited input dimensions through parameter slicing. Includes pre-built examples like shells, jellyfish, fractals, and neural networks, with support for custom JavaScript function definitions and AI-assisted generation.

recent_posts.title: Emergence and a New Kind of Science
recent_posts.summary: Explores emergence as a fundamental concept where simple building blocks following basic rules create unexpectedly complex patterns and behaviors. Uses cellular automata, Conway's Game of Life, and Wolfram's computational experiments to demonstrate how combinatorial explosions generate complexity that cannot be predicted without running the system. Discusses four categories of emergent complexity (flat, repetitive, chaotic, and organized), computational irreducibility, and practical advice for designing emergent systems through iterative experimentation rather than direct control.

recent_posts.title: Building AI bots to autonomously beat Minecraft
recent_posts.summary: Explores the challenge of creating AI bots that can autonomously complete Minecraft from start to finish, including killing the Ender Dragon. While one bot (Alto Clefft) has achieved this, most current AI implementations struggle with fundamental pathfinding and navigation issues. The author calls for community collaboration to improve bot frameworks like Mind Flare, focusing on better pathfinding algorithms, water navigation, and reliable tool usage to make fully autonomous Minecraft completion more achievable.

recent_posts.title: Evolving Brains in the Life Engine (5 Year Anniversary!)
recent_posts.summary: A developer celebrates the 5-year anniversary of their Life Engine evolution simulator with a major update featuring improved performance, enhanced brain systems using state machines, and new evolution controls. The simulator models organisms as collections of colored cells with different functions (movement, feeding, killing, protection) that evolve through natural selection. Key improvements include 2-10x speed increases through JavaScript optimization techniques, multi-state brain systems for complex behaviors, and symmetrical mutation options. The creator shares the project's origin story and discusses future plans to focus on Minecraft-related projects.

recent_posts.title: AI Self Portrait #claude #ai
recent_posts.summary: An experiment where Claude AI was given command line access to create self-portraits through code, resulting in an iterative feedback loop where the AI generates images, analyzes them, and creates new versions. The process sometimes produces unexpected, surreal results, demonstrating the unpredictable behavior that can emerge when AI agents are given autonomous control over systems.

recent_posts.title: AI Self-Portrait #gemini #ai
recent_posts.summary: An experiment where Gemini 2.5 Pro AI agent was given command line access to create self-portraits through code. The AI generated images, analyzed them, made modifications, and repeated the process in an endless feedback loop, demonstrating autonomous creative behavior when given system control.

top_posts.title: AI Agents
top_posts.summary: An experimental exploration of AI coding agents (Claude and Gemini) running autonomously in virtual environments to create generative art through code. The agents use feedback loops to generate images, view their output, and iteratively improve their creations. Multiple agents were tested working in parallel on collaborative tasks like building a virtual city, revealing both creative potential and significant limitations in multi-agent coordination. The experiments highlight current challenges with AI agent autonomy, including tendency toward grandiose self-assessment, difficulty with open-ended tasks, and substantial API costs ranging from $20-34 per day of usage.

top_posts.title: Langton's Ants and Turing Machines
top_posts.summary: Langton's Ant is a cellular automaton where an ant moves on a grid following simple rules: turn left on white cells (changing them to black) and turn right on black cells (changing them to white). Despite these basic rules, the ant exhibits complex emergent behavior, initially moving randomly before eventually creating structured patterns like highways. The concept extends to multiple ants creating collaborative behaviors and can be generalized using state machines to create universal Turing machines called 'turmites.' These systems demonstrate how simple deterministic rules can produce unpredictable, complex patterns and serve as computational models capable of universal computation.
